items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: He was a real good drummer and everything, but I never did play with him.

ctx.x: Goldston, yeah. Now, really happy. He was a real good drummer and everything, but I never did play with him. You know, I seen him at the Regal Theater there with Robichoke Bay. I thought he was a mighty good drummer. I thought he was a very good drummer. I thought he was a very good drummer.

I never met him. I heard Paul Balberin talk a lot about him. One of his favorites is not his favorite. Well, what did John McMurray play like? Isn't that his name? Mac Murray, they called it. I'm not sure of his first name. Did you know him? Mac Murray, the drummer. Did you ever know him? No. I never knew him.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: He played parade with us once.

ctx.x: On the snare drum. On the street.

Them times? Mm-hmm. I'll tell you. Henry Martin was one of the best. Mm-hmm. Well, Happy, I don't believe I've never seen him play. Yeah, I did see him play parade. He played parade with us once. Long time ago. He played nice. I had Black Benny on the bass drum. He's the bad man on the bass drum. Boy, he played more bass drum. Sure.
Now, back to the piano players. What about Manuel Bonetta? Did you ever work with him?
